record.paper_title: Answering open questions in biology using spatial genomics and structured methods
record.original_question: What is the best way to represent cellular morphology for joint analysis with spatial single-cell molecular measurements, given that gene expression is naturally represented as a count matrix but morphology lacks a universal tabular representation and may need to be encoded either as engineered features or as learned image embeddings?

evidence.quote: The primary open question here is how to best represent morphology. While gene expression is conventionally represented by a count matrix, there is not a similar universal tabular form to represent morphology.

artifact.status_search_result: The question of how best to represent cellular morphology for joint analysis with spatial single-cell omics is an active and unresolved area of research. Recent work (e.g. CellProfiler-style engineered features, deep-learning embeddings such as DINO/CLIP-based cell image encoders, and morphology-expression multimodal foundation models) explores both engineered and learned representations, but no consensus optimal representation has been established.

status_evidence.title: Answering open questions in biology using spatial genomics and structured methods
status_evidence.snippet: The primary open question here is how to best represent morphology.
status_evidence.claim: The representation of morphology for joint analysis with spatial molecular data is explicitly stated as an open question.
